newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise, ANS idle amid imports.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise, ANS idle amid imports.

text.p: Interest in U.S. West Coast crude slumped late Thursday, as a number of South American cargoes were advertized in the market, paralyzing Alaskan differentials, traders said.

South American crudes on offer included a cargo of Venezulan Tia Juana Heavy (12.3 API gravity, 2.82 sulphur), a Colombian South Blend (29, 0.8) and at least three Ecuadorean Oriente (28.8, 1.02) cargoes.
West Coast marker Alaska North Slope (ANS) last traded a week ago at $1.32 below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), which compared with a week earlier at $1.05 below.
BP Oil, the dominant seller of ANS, was offering Thursday at 95 cents below but refiners said the price remained out-of-synch with supply and demand.
Some traders said BP has recently revived its shipments of ANS east via All-American pipeline, but players surveyed could not agree on how much shipments had increased.
Traders said Oriente was being offered at competitive prices of $1.40 to $1.50 under ANS, delivered to the West Coast.
Most refineries around Los Angeles and the Bay area can run Oriente. The slightly better quality South Blend is expected to trade somewhere between Oriente and ANS price.
